paragraphs.source_en: The fact that for their paintings the pastoralists sometimes used the walls with existing Round Head paintings gives valuable information about the importance of the sites. Although the later art, dominated by domesticated animals, appeared more practical than symbolical, they evidently considered the places which were previously or still used by the hunters as special and significant. And even though they could just paint over the previous figures, they only did so on rare occasions. In cases of superimposition, they further confirm the relative chronology known from the archaeological record, and they indicate that at least some of the Round Head paintings were created before 7,500 BP.
